title: Preparation of Silicon Nanowire Field-effect Transistor for Chemical and Biosensing Applications
protocol: Prepare a 100-nm-thick thermal oxide layer on a Si substrate using wet oxidation at 980 °C for 4 hr with O2 and H2 process gas.
Deposit a 50-nm-thick nitride layer by low-pressure chemical vapor deposition at 980 °C for 4 hr.
Deposit a 100-nm-thick tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) layer by LPCVD at 780 °C for 4 hr.
Coat the wafer with an 830-nm-thick photoresist layer.
Expose the coated wafer using an I-line stepper with a pattern-defined photomask and a strength of 1,980 J.
Develop the exposed wafer within a developer for 5 min.
Perform isotropic etching by using HBr and Cl plasma gas for 1 min in a standard inductively coupled plasma etcher.
Deposit a 100-nm-thick amorphous silicon layer by LPCVD.
Anneal the deposited layer at 600 °C in N2 ambient for 24 hr to transform it into polycrystalline silicon.
Implant phosphorous ions through source/drain doping at low energy (5E15 cm−2).
Perform standard lithography using an I-line stepper to remove the poly-Si layer and form polysilicon nanowire.
Rinse the device with pure acetone.
Sonicate the device in pure acetone for 10 min using sonication (46 kHz, 80 W).
Sonicate the device in pure ethanol for 5 min using sonication (46 kHz, 80 W).
Blow-dry the surface of the device with nitrogen.
Treat the device with O2 plasma at 18 W for 30 sec.
Immerse the device in a 2.0% (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES)/ethanol solution for 30 min.
Wash the device with ethanol three times.
Sonicate the device in ethanol for 10 min using sonication (46 kHz, 80 W).
Heat the device on a hot plate at 120 °C for 10 min to create amine groups on SNWs.
Immerse the device in 12.5% glutaraldehyde for 1 hour at room temperature.
Avoid light exposure during immersion.
Wash the device with 10 mM sodium phosphate buffer (Na-PB; pH 7.0) three times.
Blow-dry the surface of the device with nitrogen.
Immerse the device in a solution containing 1 µM DNA probes overnight.
Immerse the device in 10 mM Tris buffer (pH 8.0) with 4.0 mM NaBH3CN for 30 minutes.
Wash the device with Na-PB (pH 7.0) three times.
Blow-dry the surface of the device with nitrogen.
Prepare 10 mM sodium phosphate tribasic dodecahydrate (Na3PO4) in deionized water (pH 11.60).
Prepare 10 mM phosphoric acid (H3PO4) in deionized water (pH 2.35).
Mix Na-PB with different volumes of H3PO4 buffer to obtain pH values of 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0, 8.0, and 9.0.
Measure the pH value for each prepared buffer solution.
Determine the optimal liquid gate voltage (VLG) for measurement at each modification step.
Deliver the 10 mM Na-PB (pH 7.0) solution to the SNW surface by using a syringe pump (flow rate: 5.0 ml/hr).
Measure the real-time conductance of the device while sweeping VLG from 0.80 to 1.30 V.
Perform conductance measurement by using the lock-in technique at room temperature.
Convert AC current signals into an AC voltage signal using a low-noise current preamplifier.
Collect data on conductance (G) upon increasing VLG from 0.80 to 1.30 V in intervals of 0.02 V.
Determine the optimal VLG based on maximum sensitivity.
Plot G-VLG curves and obtain the equation of the curve.
Differentiate the obtained equation at each point of VLG.
Divide the differentiated values by G to determine the optimal VLG according to the maximum number.
Measure real-time conductance changes during surface modifications using the lock-in technique at room temperature.
Convert the AC current signal into AC voltage signals using a low-noise current preamplifier.
Set the optimal VLG for each step of surface modification (step 2.2: VLG = 1.02).
Set the optimal VLG for each step of surface modification (step 3.1: VLG = 0.98).
Set the optimal VLG for each step of surface modification (step 3.2: VLG = 0.98).
Set the optimal VLG for each step of surface modification (step 3.3: VLG = 1.0).
Deliver the 10 mM Na-PB solution with pH values from 3.0 to 9.0 to the SNW surface at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr.
Collect data on conductance at a drain voltage of 0.01 V during surface modification steps.
Measure electric properties (ID-VBG curve) of the device in 10 mM Na-PB (pH 7.0) after each surface modification step.
Deliver the 10 mM Na-PB solution (pH 7.0) to the SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for direct contact with the SNW.
Select the "nMOSFET" mode on the commercial semiconductor analyzer and software.
Select "ID-VBG" modules on the commercial semiconductor analyzer and software.
Measure the ID of the device after each surface modification step using a commercial semiconductor analyzer and software.
Set a constant bias voltage of 0.5 V.
Sweep the gate potential from −1 to 3.0 V in intervals of 0.2 V.
Deliver 10 mM Na-PB solution (pH 7.0) to the DNA probe-immobilized SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Incubate the SNW for 30 minutes.
Measure the ID of the device.
Load 10 pM complementary target DNA onto the DNA probe-immobilized SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Incubate the SNW for 30 minutes.
Deliver 10 mM Na-PB solution (pH 7.0) to the SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Measure the ID of the device again.
Load 1 nM recovery DNA onto the DNA probe-immobilized SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Incubate the SNW for 30 minutes.
Deliver 10 mM Na-PB solution (pH 7.0) to the SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Measure the ID of the device one more time.
Load 100 pM non-complementary DNA onto the DNA probe-immobilized SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
Incubate the SNW with the loaded DNA for 30 minutes.
Deliver a 10 mM Na-PB solution (pH 7.0) onto the SNW surface using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 5.0 ml/hr for 10 minutes.
